dish: Teochew sliced-fish porridge and clear fish soup
n: Kwang Kee Teochew Fish Porridge (One Punggol)
address: One Punggol Hawker Centre, #02-19, Punggol, Singapore (street + postal to confirm at geocode)
w: Punggol branch of a Teochew fish-porridge stall founded in 1962 and on the MICHELIN Bib Gourmand list every year since 2021. Known for a light, clean, sweet-savoury broth and fresh fish slices; the original is at Newton Food Centre.

dish: Gravy-laden fried Hokkien mee with prawns and squid
address: Punggol Coast Hawker Centre, Punggol, Singapore (stall no. + postal to confirm at geocode)
w: MICHELIN Bib Gourmand Hokkien mee from Whampoa Drive, and the headline name when Punggol Coast Hawker Centre opened on 25 July 2025. Yellow egg noodles and bee hoon are braised in a rich prawn stock and topped with prawns and squid.

address: Punggol Coast Hawker Centre, Punggol, Singapore (stall no. + postal to confirm at geocode)
w: A braised-duck stall with about 50 years of history. It closed at Desker Road in early 2024 and came back at Punggol Coast Hawker Centre in July 2025, a comeback the local press covered as one of the openings of the year.

dish: Cantonese mixed porridge (century egg, liver, cuttlefish, you tiao)
address: One Punggol Hawker Centre, #02-14, Punggol, Singapore (street + postal to confirm at geocode)
w: Silky Cantonese congee in more than 10 versions. The signature mixed porridge comes loaded with century egg, chicken, pork liver, cuttlefish, meatball and fried you tiao. This is the second stall, after Our Tampines Hub.

dish: Penang-style rojak with fruit, vegetables and you tiao in sweet-spicy prawn paste
address: One Punggol Hawker Centre, #02-11, Punggol, Singapore (street + postal to confirm at geocode)
w: Penang-style rojak from a Malaysian family recipe: tropical fruit, crunchy vegetables and fried dough fritters tossed in a thick sweet-spicy paste. It moved here from Joo Chiat Place when One Punggol opened.
